import logging

def test_caplog_clear_get_records_consistency(caplog) -> None:
    """Test that get_records() stays consistent with records after clear()."""
    def verify_consistency() -> None:
        assert caplog.get_records("call") == caplog.records

    # Initial state: both empty
    verify_consistency()
    
    # After logging
    logging.warning("test1")
    verify_consistency()
    assert len(caplog.records) == 1
    
    # After clear
    caplog.clear()
    verify_consistency()
    assert len(caplog.records) == 0
    
    # After logging again
    logging.warning("test2")
    verify_consistency()
    assert len(caplog.records) == 1
    assert caplog.records[0].getMessage() == "test2"

def test_caplog_clear_text_reset(caplog) -> None:
    """Test that text is also reset after clear()."""
    logging.warning("test")
    assert "test" in caplog.text
    caplog.clear()
    assert caplog.text == ""
    
    # Log again
    logging.warning("test2")
    assert "test2" in caplog.text
    assert "test" not in caplog.text

def test_caplog_records_are_same_object(caplog) -> None:
    """Verify that get_records() and records return the same object."""
    logging.warning("test")
    
    # They should be the same object
    assert caplog.get_records("call") is caplog.records
    
    # After clear, they should still be the same object
    caplog.clear()
    assert caplog.get_records("call") is caplog.records
    
    # And should still be empty
    assert len(caplog.records) == 0
    assert len(caplog.get_records("call")) == 0
